messages.subject: cannot load CelSet: 'affymetrix_calvin_exceptions::DataSetNotFoundException'
parts:
Hi There,

I just added another dataset to an existing directory (where I have
processed this same chip type in the past with no problem) according
to the layout specified in :
http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/directory-structures.
I now receive the following error for the second datastet(2), while
the first is still fine and can be accessed normally.

> cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("GenomeWideSNP_6", tags="Full")

The cdf loads fine, but when I try to read in the cel files, I get the
following error:
> cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("Dataset2", chipType = "GenomeWideSNP_6", cdf = cdf)
> cs

terminate called after throwing an instance of
'affymetrix_calvin_exceptions::DataSetNotFoundException'
Aborted

- at which point R exits

Any pointers, as this doesn't make any sense since it has worked in
the past? I have also tried setting up the new dataset in a separate
directory with the appropriate annotationData as well, but this
doesn't work either. The CEL files have a similar naming scheme,
though I am not making use of annotationData/samples, do I need to?
I have upgraded to latest version of R and aroma.affymetrix, but still
get the same error.

a quick comment since I have to run:

>> cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType("GenomeWideSNP_6", tags="Full")
>
> The cdf loads fine, but when I try to read in the cel files, I get the
> following error:
>> cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("Dataset2", chipType = "GenomeWideSNP_6", cdf = cdf)

>> cs
>
> terminate called after throwing an instance of
> 'affymetrix_calvin_exceptions::DataSetNotFoundException'
> Aborted

This is a exception occurring in affxparser/Fusion SDK. We see them
rarely, and often they indicate corrupt files or incorrect file
formats. Files are read in lexicographic order. Try with only a few
CEL files; it might be that one of the files are corrupt. Compare
file sizes etc for you CEL file; sometime one is too small. If you can
narrow it down to a single CEL file (a single-CEL-file data set), if
you can post the CEL file somewhere I can have a look at it.

/Henrik
